primary_topics: CJP's Preface to 'The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary', his yearly transparency report covering his eighth year on the Supreme Court (October 10, 2002 to October 10, 2003), introducing the theme of how new biosciences and biotechnologies affect judicial decision-making

Overview of the volume's structure (judicial reform, legal education, and major SC decisions)

stances.claim: Jurists must have a working knowledge of all branches of human endeavor, not merely the codes and jurisprudence.

notable_anecdotes: He frames the yearly book as his 'small contribution to transparency.'
one_paragraph_summary: CJP's Preface to the book, his yearly 'contribution to transparency' covering his eighth year on the Supreme Court (October 10, 2002 to October 10, 2003). He introduces the theme — how the new biosciences and biotechnologies affect the judiciary's decision-making — and argues that, since 'law is a jealous mistress,' jurists must be more than 'walking computers' of the codes, needing a working knowledge of every facet of life and learning.
